title: Sparse single-orbit testers for generalized Reed–Muller codes over finite fields
author: Noga Ron-Zewi and Madhu Sudan
work: A New Upper Bound on the Query Complexity of Testing Generalized Reed-Muller Codes
source_version: Theory of Computing volume 9 article 25 (2013), official complete journal PDF acquired 2026-09-30; canonical DOI 10.4086/toc.2013.v009a025 verified against official landing and printed PDF header
difficulty_reason: Even after the named affine-family and Lucas/Kummer prerequisites, the proof must construct a divided iterated directional-difference constraint, bound its support, and prove its simultaneous acceptance and rejection behavior by finite-field power sums and carry-free coefficients. The complete authored product/union constructions at1174–1392 then preserve the explicit locality bound, while the new affine monomial-transfer proof at1398–1479 makes the entire orbit reject every border monomial. These coupled sparse-constraint and orbit-characterization obligations form one H2 task above routine finite-field interpolation or direct application of a testing theorem.
